feed.title: Analytic Madhyasth Darshan studies
feed.subtitle: Draft and released studies, newest Edited-on timestamp first. In-progress (ongoing) rows are omitted.

entry.title: The Ontology of Coexistence
entry.summary: Madhyasth Darshan's account of existence as the coexistence of satta and units — saturation, the four orders, sentience, causation, conservation, and the reality of the world — compared in depth with Advaita Vedanta and modern physics and philosophy

entry.title: From Unit Activity to Human Orderliness: A State-Dynamic Reconstruction of Coexistence
entry.summary: A synthesis of coexistence as unit activity, connecting ontology with Jeevan's concentric faculties, evaluation, values, justice, and continuous realised fulfilment. It explains how humane living extends through five social functions, universal participation, and awakened tradition, with the formal model developed in appendices.

entry.title: Why Humans Are Not Just Material
entry.summary: Whether a human being is reducible to an insentient physicochemical body: Madhyasth Darshan's body-and-jeevan account compared with scientific evidence, its physicalist interpretation, and Advaita Vedanta, followed by a critical review of all three frameworks

entry.title: The Epistemology of Coexistence
entry.summary: What knowledge is, who the knower is, and what can be known: coexistence, jeevan, humane conduct, evidence, and epistemic error — compared with Advaita Vedanta, modern Western philosophy, and natural science

entry.title: Axiology: Value Theory
entry.summary: Value as essentiality in active units: Madhyasth Darshan's forms of value, their recognition and fulfilment, what endures or changes, and the distinct senses in which values are compared

entry.title: Spiritual Practice and Realization
entry.summary: Realization and awakening in Madhyasth Darshan: anubhav, samyama, upasana, and liberation from mystery, compared with Advaita Vedanta and with modern philosophy of religious experience and contemplative science

entry.title: Nature of Time
entry.summary: What time (kaal) is: the duration of unit-activity against timeless satta, numerical reckoning, and the past–present–future structure — compared with Advaita Vedanta, the philosophy of time, and physics (spacetime, cosmology, entropy)

entry.title: Human Behavior and Society
entry.summary: Humane conduct and social organisation in Madhyasth Darshan, compared with the natural sciences, Advaita Vedanta, and religious and technocratic approaches

entry.title: How to Form Self-Sustaining Organizations
entry.summary: Examines Madhyasth Darshan's claim that organisations grounded in fear or accumulation become extractive, and its account of organisations that sustain themselves without instrumentalising their members

entry.title: How Undivided Society Is Established
entry.summary: Madhyasth Darshan's account of how undivided society is established through coexistence, justice, family, institutions, and education — compared with science-only materialism, Advaita Vedanta, and Hindu religious authority

entry.title: Family Relationships and Values
entry.summary: The family as the first site of values: recognising relationships and living trust, affection, gratitude, and mutual satisfaction

entry.title: Ethics and Morals in Human Beings
entry.summary: Whether ethics is divine command, convention, evolution, reason, or evidence of understanding: Madhyasth Darshan's account of humane conduct through justice, dharma, truth, and right-use, compared with Advaita Vedanta and modern moral science

entry.title: Aesthetics
entry.summary: What beauty and art are: Madhyasth Darshan's functional aesthetics of usefulness, harmony, and human purpose, compared with modern philosophical aesthetics and Advaita Vedanta
